§9.7.2 Footnotes Inside the Frame

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

tables-footnotes-inside-the-frame · tables captions boundaries

✅ Normative

A table footnote MUST be rendered outside the table, as footnote text placed after it — even when the page prints it inside the table's ruled border. It MUST NOT be rendered as a row of the table. It retains the Footnote class and MUST NOT be wrapped in <caption>. This is a deliberate exception to the frame test.

A footnote line printed within the table's own ruled border:

| Rate A     | 1.10¹   |
| Rate B     | 1.25    |
| ¹ Excludes riders    |   ← printed INSIDE the ruled frame

Why the frame test does not decide footnotes

The frame test — ink inside the border is a row, ink outside it is a caption — decides titles and banners in Titles Banners Captions§9.7.3 and totals blocks in Bottom Edge Totals and Islands§9.7.1. It is worth having because it is mechanical.

A footnote is where it gives the wrong answer. The line names no columns and carries no values, so rendering it as a row asserts something false about the table: a consumer counting records gets one too many, and the row's single cell has no relationship to any column above it. Where the typesetter drew the border is a layout accident — the footnote is commentary on the table either way.

The carve-out costs the frame test its single-signal property, and that price is paid deliberately: the frame decides titles and banners; it does not decide footnotes.

✅ Sample — wwa

(Justify Selection and Trend Period in Filing Memorandum) is printed inside the table's grid, under the last data row — the case where the frame test and instinct disagree. It is set in italics, and it follows the table as footnote text.

Rendering the footnote

  • Wherever the border falls, the footnote MUST be footnote text placed immediately after the table. It MUST be transcribed verbatim, including its leading marker, and MUST stay attached to the table it annotates rather than drifting into the surrounding prose.
  • A line opening ¹, *, (a) or Note: that refers to a marker printed in a cell above it is a footnote, not a row.
  • Superscript markers inside cells MUST stay attached to their values — see Marks and Symbols in Cells§9.6.6. The footnote body leaving the table does not take the reference with it, so 1.10¹ in the cell and ¹ Excludes riders after the table still point at each other.
  • The text MUST survive either way. Only its placement is decided here; dropping it is never conforming.

✅ Sample — two footnotes inside a shaded frame

Footnotes 1 and 2 sit inside the grey-bordered panel that frames the trading table, under the Total row, in a smaller face. Both follow the table as footnote text; the superscript markers stay in the header cells and the Other trading label. Only the year band and the Total row are printed bold; the hyphenated header wraps (per- / form- / ance) are joined.
